newsitem.title: UK: Dry weather hampers Europe beet development -Licht.
newsitem.headline: Dry weather hampers Europe beet development -Licht.

text.p: Dry weather in much of Europe has helped farmers to sow the 1997/98 sugar beet crop, but seed development is starting to suffer, analyst F.O. Licht said on Wednesday.

In its daily report, Licht said sowings in Western Europe had progressed better than normal during the past week, but the lack of rains in France and Britain was beginning to hamper early plant development.
The main improvement in the week ended April 22 was in Spain, where rains improved germination conditions.
Moisture was more prevalent in central and eastern Europe but the potential for crop benefit was being countered by freezing temperatures, Licht said.
"Freezing weather in some central and eastern states could have damaged beets in isolated areas. However, there is still plenty of time for replanting," it said.
"The eastern European areas continue to have favourable moisture for good early growth but it has been slowed by the cooler than normal weather."

Licht cited recent reports from Serbia, where sugar producers fear that more frost could affect beets already re-sown on an area of some 10,000 ha. Re-sowing would raise costs and late planting would affect yields.
